nodes.rationale: Each scene carries a single claim: symbols are introduced first, then the state, then the change and result, and several unfamiliar symbols are never added at the same time.

nodes.rationale: Template-specific rules (color use, diagram shape, graph style, post-build checks) are owned by each template's DESIGN.md, so the skill itself keeps no per-template conventions.

nodes.label: Motion necessity test
nodes.rationale: GIFs are made only on request. Before animating, write in one sentence which direction, order, speed or concurrency information a static figure would lose; if the presenter must pause at every step, several static states may serve better, and that static alternative is suggested in one line of the report.

nodes.label: Chart text size and slot-shrink inspection
nodes.norm_label: chart text size and slot-shrink inspection
nodes.rationale: The build shrinks figures to fit their slot, and its overflow check and the audit crops do not read text inside figures, so wide charts and grid placements end up with smaller real text; the enlarged preview PNG is therefore inspected, and labels are shortened instead of shrinking fonts.

nodes.label: Agent downloads go to figures/external/
nodes.rationale: sources/ holds the researcher's original material, so adding files there releases approvals from Stage 1, whereas changes under figures/ only require re-checking Stage 4; PDFs the agent downloads therefore go to figures/external/.

nodes.label: Internal versus public-use image policy
nodes.rationale: Internal talks need no per-photo approval because photos join the Stage 3 figure plan and Stage 4 content review; public or distributed talks prefer assets with checkable usage terms and report unclear images for confirmation. Web photos show a target or environment and are never described as the presenter's own experiment results.

nodes.label: Three creation tiers: automatic, in-scope, request
nodes.norm_label: three creation tiers: automatic, in-scope, request
nodes.rationale: Redrawn flows, timelines, matrices and cards are made without asking because they carry no new values; numeric charts, new result graphs and GIFs are made within the requested scope without re-asking per figure; numbers, errors or results with no source data are never fabricated and stay as requests, and synthetic teaching examples are labelled synthetic.

nodes.label: Task inputs outrank external skills
nodes.rationale: External skills may re-ask about audience or style or try to build a standalone talk, but this task's inputs, preset and approvals take priority; data and transformations are tied to code, diagram inputs, outputs and arrow meanings are verified, and without execution tools the static work proceeds and the need to install is reported.

nodes.label: Common frontmatter fields for stage documents
nodes.norm_label: common frontmatter fields for stage documents
nodes.rationale: schema_version, task_id, stage, status, approval_hash and upstream_hashes are required; assumptions and open_items default to empty; duplicate keys, wrong types, NaN and mismatched task IDs are rejected.

nodes.label: Effective status values: missing, draft, approved, stale, invalid
nodes.norm_label: effective status values: missing, draft, approved, stale, invalid

nodes.label: `content_hash` versus `review_hash`
nodes.rationale: review_hash binds the document content hash to the current upstream input hashes, so approval is refused if source material changed after review; `--expected-hash` carries the reviewed value.

nodes.label: Input hashing of `sources/` and `figures/`
nodes.rationale: Stage 1 hashes sources/; Stages 2-4 add earlier stage content hashes; Stage 4 adds figures/; symlinks are rejected.

nodes.label: Stage 1 `plan/interview.md` review fields
nodes.rationale: review holds audience, purpose, key_evidence, success_criteria, constraints and optional tutorial.prerequisites; blocking open items must be resolved or the claim narrowed before approval.

nodes.label: Stage 2 `plan/brief.md` message candidates
nodes.rationale: One to three candidates; the selected candidate's message and storyline must equal the final key_message and storyline.

nodes.label: Stage 3 `plan/outline.md` slide entries
nodes.rationale: review.slides needs id, topic, headline, evidence, seconds; section and figure are optional; total seconds over duration_minutes raises a warning only.

nodes.label: Stage 4 `slides.md` deck frontmatter
nodes.rationale: deck holds title, subtitle, date, presenter, affiliation, `preset` (default rvlab) and `budget`; review.language is ko or en; the build selects the template from `deck.preset`.

nodes.label: Tutorial `requires`/`provides` dependency warnings
nodes.rationale: Only for tasks whose Stage 1 has review.tutorial; a requires not covered by prerequisites or an earlier provides raises a warning, not a block.

nodes.label: `default_budget` optional work scale
nodes.rationale: One of quick, standard or thorough.

nodes.label: `default_preset` optional design preset
nodes.rationale: One of rvlab, modern-minimal, retro or neo-city (list via `uv run pptgen presets`).

nodes.label: Presenter name and affiliation fields
nodes.rationale: Copied by `pptgen new` (or `rvppt new`) into each new deck's slides.md `deck` block so they can be edited per presentation.

nodes.label: Design presets: rvlab, modern-minimal, retro, neo-city
nodes.norm_label: design presets: rvlab, modern-minimal, retro, neo-city
nodes.rationale: `rvlab` (default, 4:3) is the RVLAB lab template; the other three are 16:9 (white minimal, cream serif retro, dark neon neo-city).

nodes.label: Hash checks content identity, not user consent
nodes.norm_label: hash checks content identity, not user consent
nodes.rationale: The agent calls approve only after the user's explicit approval.

nodes.label: Pinned Python and Node dependencies
nodes.rationale: python-pptx, lxml, PyYAML, Pillow, PyMuPDF and pypandoc-binary locked in uv.lock; MathJax, Mermaid CLI and resvg locked in package-lock.json; LibreOffice is external.

nodes.label: Markdown to Pandoc AST to PPTX to LibreOffice QA
nodes.norm_label: markdown to pandoc ast to pptx to libreoffice qa
nodes.rationale: Markdown to Pandoc AST and native blocks to python-pptx/XML fixed layout to LibreOffice render QA.

nodes.label: RVLAB master, logo, and theme preservation
nodes.norm_label: rvlab master, logo, and theme preservation
nodes.rationale: The derived reference keeps the original master, logo, theme and decoration, adds seven Pandoc layout names and a fixed figure grid, and strips only sample slides, presenter, date, notes and Google metadata; the `type` attribute of `p:ph` is omitted so Pandoc finds body placeholders.

nodes.label: 16:9 themes styled by DESIGN.md `style` blocks
nodes.rationale: modern-minimal, retro and neo-city share the same placeholder structure; dark themes take body, table, equation image, Mermaid and chart colors from palette `text` and `background`.

nodes.label: `pptgen anatomy` isometric diagram build
nodes.rationale: Builds a 300-DPI PNG, standalone SVG and interactive HTML in one run using the vendored anatomy skill.

nodes.label: `pptgen audit` 4x close-up critic loop
nodes.rationale: Thumbnails alone never pass; key sentences, formulas, GIF frames, captions and sources are cropped at 4x and checked for box margins and luminance contrast.

nodes.label: Up-front sizing with `--budget`
nodes.rationale: Presentation and visual scale (quick, standard, thorough) is agreed at the start of work.

nodes.label: `register-template` custom PPTX registration
nodes.rationale: Imports only the input PPTX size and colors; layout, logo and background are not carried over.

nodes.label: Truth-first `plan/PROGRESS.md` record
nodes.rationale: Source formulas, numbers, invariants and cross-session progress are recorded in plan/PROGRESS.md.

nodes.label: Font fallback changes line breaks
nodes.rationale: Substituting fonts (Arial to Liberation Sans, Malgun Gothic to Noto Sans CJK KR) changes wrapping, so rendering and overflow checks run with the actually selected fonts.

nodes.label: PowerPoint rendering not yet verified
nodes.rationale: QA is LibreOffice-based; passing with LibreOffice and fallback fonts does not guarantee PowerPoint layout; platform verification scope is recorded in the build report.

nodes.label: Known limits of templates and render QA
nodes.norm_label: known limits of templates and render qa
nodes.rationale: register-template does not carry layout; render QA uses LibreOffice with the selected fonts and PowerPoint rendering is not yet verified.

nodes.label: Project skills and their roles table
nodes.norm_label: project skills and their roles table

nodes.label: Five project skills and `pptgen` command
nodes.rationale: Skills: ppt-interview, ppt-maker, ppt-charts, ppt-animation, ppt-tutorial; `rvppt` is the legacy command name.

nodes.label: ppt-maker skill for Stage 4 writing and building
nodes.norm_label: ppt-maker skill for stage 4 writing and building

nodes.label: Audience-first fit judgment order
nodes.rationale: The preset fixes only layout, fonts and color, so the agent judges what and how much to show: audience and purpose in plan/interview.md first, then the template's DESIGN.md, then consistency within the deck; when the first two conflict the audience wins and the judgment is written in the Stage 4 report. Lint warnings are advisory while real overflow is blocked by the build.

nodes.label: slides.md is the source of truth
nodes.norm_label: slides.md is the source of truth
nodes.rationale: slides.md is the original and the PPTX and PDF are build outputs, so problems are fixed in slides.md or the figure sources and rebuilt rather than by editing the result file.

nodes.label: Beginner follow-along critic before approval
nodes.rationale: The author already knows the content and cannot see its gaps, so a fresh subagent that has not read the sources and sees only slides.md and review.tutorial.prerequisites lists where a learner would get stuck; findings are logged with a [tutorial] tag in the Critic Loop, and the critic does not replace testing with a real learner.

nodes.label: Four items every hands-on slide carries
nodes.norm_label: four items every hands-on slide carries
nodes.rationale: A learner reading alone may not see ::: notes, so everything needed to follow along (where, what, what should appear, what to do on failure) is placed in the slide body rather than only in the notes.

nodes.label: No invented commands, paths, or outputs
nodes.norm_label: no invented commands, paths, or outputs
nodes.rationale: Install commands, paths, filenames and expected outputs are written only when confirmed in the source material or the user's own run; gaps are left as unresolved items or capture requests instead of being invented.

nodes.label: Agent-judged wording, structure, and emphasis
nodes.rationale: Sentences, tone, composition, length, bullets, tables, accent colors and figure impressions are the agent's call; lint warnings are advisory.

nodes.label: Code-enforced limits on unrenderable input and overflow
nodes.norm_label: code-enforced limits on unrenderable input and overflow
nodes.rationale: Blocks inputs the renderer cannot honor (merged cells, arbitrary coordinates or sizes, figures outside the task, LaTeX macro definitions) and measured overflow; overflow is fixed by splitting or trimming.

nodes.label: `templates/<id>/DESIGN.md` style contract
nodes.rationale: Skills load the DESIGN.md of `deck.preset` at start; template-only style rules (color use, diagram shape, graph style, cover checks) live there, not in skills. Fit is judged by audience and purpose, then DESIGN.md, then deck consistency.

nodes.label: Approval only via `pptgen approve` after user consent
nodes.norm_label: approval only via `pptgen approve` after user consent

nodes.label: `graphify-out/` as non-authoritative structure reference
nodes.rationale: Actual code wins over the graph; real task content must never be fed to Graphify.

nodes.label: Preset-decided layout, fonts, and base colors
nodes.norm_label: preset-decided layout, fonts, and base colors
nodes.rationale: Cover, TOC, section and thank-you slides are generated by the build; tokens come from the first YAML block of the template DESIGN.md.

nodes.label: Protected originals: `sources/`, RVLAB template, external skills
nodes.norm_label: protected originals: `sources/`, rvlab template, external skills

nodes.label: Edit `slides.md` or figure sources, never the PPTX
nodes.norm_label: edit `slides.md` or figure sources, never the pptx
nodes.rationale: The result PPTX is rebuilt from slides.md and figure originals.

nodes.label: Form is preset, content is judgment
nodes.norm_label: form is preset, content is judgment
nodes.rationale: Splits responsibility between code, preset and agent so unrenderable input is blocked while content decisions stay with the agent.

nodes.label: No fabricated figures, quotes, or personal data
nodes.norm_label: no fabricated figures, quotes, or personal data
nodes.rationale: Illustrative example data must be stated as synthetic.

nodes.label: Template-specific style rules live in DESIGN.md
nodes.norm_label: template-specific style rules live in design.md
nodes.rationale: Skills stay template-neutral; each reads the DESIGN.md of the task's `deck.preset` at start, so style rules that vary by template are not duplicated in skills.

nodes.label: Build pipeline with LibreOffice render QA
nodes.norm_label: build pipeline with libreoffice render qa
nodes.rationale: Builds in a temp folder under .build/, checks package integrity, slide size, master, branding, figure DPI, text measurement and PDF text loss or clipping, and replaces .build/output only on success.

nodes.label: Two-column and figure grid layouts
nodes.rationale: Layout is inferred from content: a columns block gives two columns, 2-4 standalone figures give a grid, anything else is body.

nodes.label: Missing-figure request placeholders
nodes.rationale: A figure path that does not exist yet becomes a dotted box with the request text; `missing_figures` in lint and the build report lists them.

nodes.label: GIF with representative PNG pair
nodes.rationale: The PPTX keeps original GIF bytes while a separate presentation-preview-copy.pptx swaps in the same-size PNG for PDF and PNG output; PowerPoint slideshow playback is not verified by automatic QA.

nodes.label: Section, topic, key-sentence heading hierarchy
nodes.rationale: `#` section slide and TOC Chapter, `##` topic shown in the top bar and TOC, `###` key sentence is one slide; all body text sits under `###`.

nodes.label: LaTeX math as OMML plus image fallback
nodes.norm_label: latex math as omml plus image fallback
nodes.rationale: The editable PPTX stores OMML with Cambria Math plus a compatible image; the compat PPTX and PDF show 300-dpi images; edits are made in the LaTeX source.

nodes.label: `slides.md` as editable source of truth
nodes.rationale: Works like Overleaf's main.tex: researchers and agents co-edit one source and can recompile (build) at any time.

nodes.label: `content_approved` flag separate from render QA
nodes.rationale: True only when all four stages are validly approved; independent of design and render QA results.

nodes.label: No coordinates, sizes, fonts, or arbitrary classes
nodes.norm_label: no coordinates, sizes, fonts, or arbitrary classes
nodes.rationale: Layout comes from preset slots; font size is never reduced to fit content, so overflow is fixed by splitting or trimming text.

nodes.label: Hand-edited PPTX overwrite guard
nodes.rationale: Build stops if the output PPTX or PDF differs from the last build, so manual PowerPoint edits are never overwritten; .build/.lock prevents concurrent builds.

nodes.label: Initial install with `uv sync` and `npm ci`
nodes.norm_label: initial install with `uv sync` and `npm ci`
nodes.rationale: Requires Python 3.11-3.14, uv, Node 22+, LibreOffice and Korean and English fonts; Python and Node packages are lockfile-pinned and external skills are vendored.

nodes.label: Local diagrams via `beautiful-mermaid` and resvg
nodes.rationale: Installed by `npm ci`; no MCP server, browser, external account or API key; independent of the visual extra.

nodes.label: OS-specific tool installation table
nodes.rationale: Agents must show the command and reason and get user confirmation before sudo or system installs.

nodes.label: `pptgen doctor` read-only environment check
nodes.rationale: Checks Python, Pandoc, templates, external skill hashes, LibreOffice, fonts and Node renderers; no network, no file changes; exit code 2 when a required item fails; Mermaid browser and profile.yaml are optional.

nodes.label: Preset-specific font requirements
nodes.rationale: Sans presets prefer Arial and Malgun Gothic with Liberation Sans and Noto Sans CJK KR fallbacks; `retro` needs Liberation Serif (or DejaVu Serif) and Noto Serif CJK KR; actual fonts are logged in build-report.json.

nodes.label: Skill entry symlinks and Windows developer mode
nodes.norm_label: skill entry symlinks and windows developer mode
nodes.rationale: `.claude/skills/`, `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/agents/` are symlinks into `skills/`; if cloned as text files agents cannot find project skills.

nodes.label: `beautiful-mermaid` 1.1.3 local renderer
nodes.rationale: Pinned in package.json and package-lock.json; used by ppt-charts.

nodes.label: Optional `visual` tools and their licenses
nodes.rationale: Manim CE, Matplotlib and SciencePlots create figure assets only; doctor's visual_tools check is read-only and never blocks ordinary builds.

nodes.label: LF line endings for stable hashes
nodes.norm_label: lf line endings for stable hashes
nodes.rationale: External skill hashes and stage approval hashes use LF bytes, so .gitattributes pins checkout line endings to LF.

nodes.label: LibreOffice render as common QA baseline
nodes.norm_label: libreoffice render as common qa baseline
nodes.rationale: All OSes use the same LibreOffice rendering for previews and overflow checks; PowerPoint editing and display, including OMML, are not verified.

nodes.label: Personal `profile.yaml` excluded from Git
nodes.rationale: The example is copied to profile.yaml, a personal file kept out of version control.

nodes.label: plan/ documents: interview, brief, outline, PROGRESS
nodes.norm_label: plan/ documents: interview, brief, outline, progress

nodes.label: Truth Model in plan/PROGRESS.md
nodes.rationale: Confirmed formulas, values, comparison conditions, units and invariants are recorded before figures or slides are planned, so later figures and animations use only those values.

nodes.label: Talk types and section orders
nodes.rationale: The structures are starting points derived from four real RVLAB talks (kept in the local, repository-excluded templates/examples/) and are shortened or changed to fit the audience and purpose.

nodes.label: TOC skeleton from sections and topics
nodes.norm_label: toc skeleton from sections and topics

nodes.norm_label: heading levels and korean sentence style

nodes.label: Entry only for follow-along tutorials
nodes.rationale: Follow-along takes several times as many slides as an overview of the same scope, so review.tutorial is written only after the user agrees to follow-along in Stage 1; overview talks, concept lectures, paper reviews and progress reports do not use this skill.

nodes.label: Fits and avoids for lab research talks
nodes.norm_label: fits and avoids for lab research talks

nodes.norm_label: talk-type section structures and slide quality

nodes.label: interview.md four-way separation
nodes.rationale: Source facts, user requirements, agent inferences and unresolved items are kept apart so an inference is never recorded as a requirement before the user agrees; unknowns that would change the core claim are marked blocking: true in open_items.

nodes.label: Question modes: co-create, essentials, instant draft
nodes.norm_label: question modes: co-create, essentials, instant draft
nodes.rationale: Chosen in the first question batch: co-create asks for user-only knowledge in later stages, essentials proceeds on recommendations after Stage 1, instant draft fills Stages 1-3 at once and builds a draft; unconfirmed premises are never recorded as agreed.

nodes.norm_label: sync preset and budget to slides.md

nodes.norm_label: interview question guide for unconfirmed intent

nodes.label: Separate training metrics from evaluation
nodes.rationale: A claim such as 'loss falls so success rate rises' mixes a training signal with independent evaluation results, so the two are separated and the scope of the message is confirmed.

nodes.label: Skipped questions are not approval
nodes.rationale: When asked to ask fewer questions, existing evidence is reused and a recommendation, assumptions and unresolved items are shown; omitting a question is never treated as approval.

nodes.label: Mermaid flowcharts with preset styling
nodes.rationale: Rendered in strict mode with preset colors and fonts; .mmd, SVG and PNG are kept in .build/output/generated-assets/; `click` does not work.

nodes.label: Statement, number, quote slide kinds for rhythm
nodes.norm_label: statement, number, quote slide kinds for rhythm
nodes.rationale: Repeating the same slide shape tires the audience, so statement, number and quote slides are mixed in only where one sentence is the protagonist; there is no fixed frequency, and tables are used only when there are values to compare.

nodes.label: ppt-charts skill for diagrams and decorative charts
nodes.norm_label: ppt-charts skill for diagrams and decorative charts

nodes.label: Truth Model grounded motion and numbers
nodes.norm_label: truth model grounded motion and numbers
nodes.rationale: Motion and numbers must come from the Truth Model in plan/PROGRESS.md and real computation; a beautified trajectory must not be used to claim convergence or success, a GIF request does not license inventing data, and synthetic teaching examples are labelled synthetic in caption and notes.

nodes.label: Read deck.preset DESIGN.md first
nodes.rationale: Template-specific rules (color use, diagram shape, graph style, post-build checks) are owned by each template's DESIGN.md, so the skill itself keeps no per-template conventions.

nodes.label: One chart per slide, sourced values
nodes.norm_label: one chart per slide, sourced values
nodes.rationale: One chart per slide lets the key sentence serve as that chart's conclusion; values, ratios and order are used only when confirmed in the sources, and illustrative values are captioned as synthetic examples.

nodes.label: Reconstruct only approved claims
nodes.rationale: The renderer handles layout while the agent interprets content, so diagrams only restructure approved claims, nodes and relations and never add research results or unconfirmed causality.

nodes.label: No decorative branches or loops
nodes.rationale: Order-only content gets a short pipeline, group distinction gets group containers and time order gets a sequence diagram; branches or loops are never invented just to decorate.

nodes.label: Restricted syntax with single :::focus
nodes.rationale: Color and shape come from the preset palette, so style, classDef, linkStyle, config frontmatter, external links, icons and HTML are unsupported and emphasis is limited to a single :::focus.

nodes.label: Relation-first diagram design rules
nodes.rationale: A diagram should expose the one relation worth explaining (order, decision, parallel inputs, group, interaction), so content is not forced into uniform horizontal box rows, no arrow is added that the source does not confirm, and only a single core step is emphasized with :::focus.

nodes.label: Korean polish before approval request
nodes.rationale: Korean decks are polished before the approval request unless the user declines.

nodes.label: Over-polish similarity threshold near 0.7
nodes.rationale: A similarity below roughly 0.7 suggests over-polishing and must be explained in the Stage 4 report together with a summary of the changed sentences from git diff --no-index.

nodes.label: Polish does not replace content approval
nodes.norm_label: polish does not replace content approval
nodes.rationale: Polishing the wording is not a substitute for the user's explicit content approval.

nodes.label: Default Korean polish before Stage 4 approval
nodes.norm_label: default korean polish before stage 4 approval
nodes.rationale: Korean decks are polished before the Stage 4 approval request even when nobody asks; English decks (review.language: en) skip it and the user may decline.

nodes.label: Structure and facts preserved during polish
nodes.norm_label: structure and facts preserved during polish
nodes.rationale: Polishing may change only style, rhythm and wording: section and topic lines, block markers, table structure, math, code, image paths, links, citations and all numbers, units, proper nouns and English technical terms stay fixed, while key sentences may be polished without changing claim scope or numbers.

nodes.rationale: Writes only under .build/editorial/papers/ and never overwrites originals or earlier results; no layout extension, OCR or model weights are installed; scans, complex panels and formulas are verified against rendered original pages.

nodes.rationale: Mathpix (paid external API, needs consent), Nougat (code MIT, weights CC-BY-NC), Marker (Apache-2.0 code, modified OpenRAIL-M model); output is checked against the source image and never confirmed automatically.

nodes.rationale: Run on demand via uvx; layout and editability of PPT, DOCX and XLSX output are not guaranteed.

nodes.rationale: PyMuPDF and PyMuPDF4LLM are AGPL-3.0 or commercial dual-licensed and Pandoc is GPL, so these tools must not be described as MIT.

nodes.rationale: `{.statement}`, `{.number}` and `{.quote}` give varied short-text slides; sizes and colors come from DESIGN.md `slide_kinds`; no math or lists.

nodes.rationale: Passing automatic checks does not guarantee the slides communicate, and thumbnails miss cropped or tiny text, so slide PNGs are viewed directly and 4x audit crops are inspected; if the result PPTX was hand-edited the build stops instead of overwriting it.

nodes.label: Five-section character and conventions
nodes.rationale: The five sections (character, fits, avoids, figure impression, post-build checks) are not rules but a starting point for the agent's judgment of whether something fits the template.

nodes.norm_label: template folder structure and design.md contract

nodes.label: Read deck.preset DESIGN.md first
nodes.rationale: Template-specific rules (color use, diagram shape, graph style, post-build checks) are owned by each template's DESIGN.md, so the skill itself keeps no per-template conventions.

nodes.label: Edit DESIGN.md, not generated reference.pptx
nodes.rationale: reference.pptx and preview.* are generated artifacts, so DESIGN.md is edited instead; the reference.pptx of non-rvlab templates is rebuilt from DESIGN.md on every build, while previews and the rvlab reference are regenerated with python -m rvppt.template.

nodes.label: Template-specific rules live in DESIGN.md
nodes.rationale: Skills read the DESIGN.md of the task's deck.preset when they start, so rules that apply to only one template (color use, diagram shape, graph style, post-build checks) are written there instead of in the skills.

nodes.label: Audience overrides design conventions
nodes.rationale: The criteria are a basis for judging fit; when they conflict with the audience and purpose the audience is followed and the judgment is stated in the report.

nodes.label: One claim per slide, no auto font shrink
nodes.norm_label: one claim per slide, no auto font shrink
nodes.rationale: Each slide carries one claim as its key sentence and fonts are never automatically shrunk, so overflow is solved by cutting the message or splitting the slide.

nodes.label: Fixed token body for template generator
nodes.norm_label: fixed token body for template generator
nodes.rationale: The first YAML block is the fixed token body read by the derived-template generator and the build, so coordinate, font and color tokens are never copied into presentation input; a token change is a template change that requires regenerating reference and preview with python -m rvppt.template --preset rvlab and rerunning the tests.

nodes.label: Original PPTX pinned, derived layouts added
nodes.norm_label: original pptx pinned, derived layouts added
nodes.rationale: The original lab PPTX (pinned by SHA-256) and its layouts are never modified; the derived reference only removes sample slides, notes and Google metadata and adds Pandoc-named layouts, keeping the logo, blue band, yellow subtitle, decorations and theme, and the body-layout top bar title cell is not widened and its blue line is not moved.

nodes.label: Prohibitions and LibreOffice-based render QA
nodes.rationale: Arbitrary coordinates, automatic font shrinking, stretching and unauthorized cropping are banned, and emphasis colors and decoration are used only when they help delivery; contrast, sources, fonts, image resolution, slide bounds and text overflow are checked on actual renders, with QA relying on LibreOffice and installed fonts because PowerPoint rendering is not yet verified.

nodes.label: Six-step agent revision procedure
nodes.rationale: Intake, impact decision, edit, verify and report, stage approval, then QA and completion.

nodes.label: Handling broad requests like 'make it cleaner'
nodes.norm_label: handling broad requests like 'make it cleaner'
nodes.rationale: The agent names concrete problems and fixes, keeps purpose, message and numbers, and asks short choices only when interpretations diverge.

nodes.label: `plan/contracts.md` snapshot via `pptgen plan`
nodes.rationale: A view of existing approval documents at command time, not a separate approval system; Mermaid graph plus table; `pptgen status` stays read-only.

nodes.label: Change type to re-review stage table
nodes.norm_label: change type to re-review stage table
nodes.rationale: Typos and figure swaps restart at Stage 4; slide add, remove or reorder at Stage 3; message changes at Stage 2; audience, purpose or sources at Stage 1.

nodes.label: Natural-language revision requests by page, topic, or ID
nodes.norm_label: natural-language revision requests by page, topic, or id
nodes.rationale: Users say where and how to change; page numbers include auto-generated cover, TOC and section pages, so the agent maps them to real body IDs instead of subtracting a fixed offset.

nodes.label: Revision report format
nodes.rationale: Before-to-after change, kept agreements, stages to re-review, remaining issues and checks actually run; judgeable without opening files.

nodes.label: Explicit user approval with `review_hash`
nodes.rationale: A 'yes' to another question, picking a recommendation or elapsed time never counts; `approve --expected-hash` refuses if the document or upstream inputs changed since review; re-approving a stage resets later stages to draft.

nodes.label: Stage 1: situation, intent, assumptions
nodes.rationale: interview.md review: audience, purpose, key_evidence, success_criteria, constraints; separates fact, request, assumption and open item.

nodes.label: Stage 2: key message selection
nodes.rationale: brief.md compares evidence-backed message and storyline candidates with a recommendation and proposes cover title and subtitle.

nodes.label: Stage 3: outline and claim-evidence mapping
nodes.rationale: outline.md lists ID, section, topic, headline, evidence, seconds and figure plan; warns when estimated time exceeds the talk length.

nodes.label: Stage 4: content, polish, production QA
nodes.rationale: slides.md follows the rendering syntax; changes versus the approved outline appear as status warnings and go into the Stage 4 report.

nodes.label: Chat stage report format
nodes.rationale: Reports are written in chat, not as bare file links, so the user can decide without opening files; Stage 3 reports volume, cover and TOC, slide table, figure requests and open questions.

nodes.label: `pptgen status` read-only stage status
nodes.rationale: Reports next_stage, next_document, per-stage issues and warnings, assumptions and open items as JSON; valid approvals are not re-requested.

nodes.label: Task folder locations and who writes them
nodes.norm_label: task folder locations and who writes them
nodes.rationale: slides.md is the source (like Overleaf main.tex); sources/ is read-only and Git-excluded; plan/ holds interview, brief, outline, contracts, revisions and PROGRESS; .build/ holds previews, reports and intermediates.

nodes.label: Presentation production workflow and approval rules
nodes.norm_label: presentation production workflow and approval rules

nodes.label: Revision requests are not content approval
nodes.norm_label: revision requests are not content approval
nodes.rationale: A change request, option answer or 'please fix' never records approval; writing 'approved' in revisions.md approves nothing.

nodes.label: Reverts handled as new revisions
nodes.rationale: Restore the source change and re-check `status`; never copy old approval fields or hashes or overwrite the source with a regenerated PPTX.

nodes.label: Auxiliary docs excluded from approval hashes
nodes.norm_label: auxiliary docs excluded from approval hashes
nodes.rationale: contracts.md, revisions.md and PROGRESS.md carry no approval frontmatter and cannot change approval state.

nodes.label: Office Hours and brainstorming inspirations
nodes.rationale: Adapts evidence-seeking, premise-checking and alternative comparison from gstack Office Hours and situation exploration from superpowers brainstorming; uses question batches rather than one question at a time; sources referenced only by pinned-commit links.

nodes.label: Source changes invalidate earlier stages
nodes.rationale: Changes to sources/ restart review at Stage 1 and changes to figures/ restart at Stage 4.
